title: The Hunchback of Notre Dame
tagline: Ring the bells. Ring the dinner bell.
about: A kind bell-ringer hidden in Notre Dame sneaks out to the Festival of Fools in Paris.

sugar1 lemonWhisk the flour, eggs and milk into a smooth batter.Rest the batter.Cook thin crepes in a pan, brushing it with the butter between each one.Fill half with ham and gruyere, fold and warm rest with chopped tomato, torn basil and salt.Hugo, Victor and Laverne's croque bitesThe three gargoyles cheering Quasimodo onHow to make itAs written, serves 4Little ham and gruyère toasties smothered in béchamel and grilled until bubbling and blistered, cut into bites with cornichons.Melt 20g butter, stir in 1 tbsp plain flour, then whisk in 200ml milk and cook until thick, and season with nutmeg.Spread 4 slices of bread with Dijon mustard, top with 150g ham and 80g grated gruyère, and close with 4 more slices.Toast in a buttered pan for 2 minutes a side.Spread the tops with it150g bacon, diced1.2kg beef chuck, diced2 tbsp olive oil12 baby onions, peeled300g mushrooms2 tbsp plain flour2 tbsp tomato paste750ml beef stock1 tbsp red w​ine vinegar4 sprigs of thyme2 bay leaves1kg potatoes60g butter100ml milkDice the bacon and beef and peel the baby onions.Brown the bacon in the oil, then the beef in batches.Add the onions and mushrooms and colour lightly.Stir in the flour and tomato paste, then add the stock, vinegar, thyme and bay leaves.Cover and simmer gently until the beef is tender.Peel and boil the potatoes, then mash with butter and warm milk.Serve the braise over the mash.Clopin's garlic and olive chickenThe hidden Court of MiraclesHow to make itAs written, serves 4Chicken thighs braised with garlic, green olives, lemon and herbs until tender and saucy, with crusty bread to mop it all up.Season 1kg chicken thighs and brown skin side down in olive oil for 6 minutes, then turn.Add 10 whole peeled garlic cloves, 100g green olives, 1 sliced lemon,
